Topic: The Geometry of High-Dimensional Spheres: Beyond 3D

Target audience: University students with a basic background in calculus and linear algebra.

Section: section_1 — Prerequisites: The N-Dimensional Coordinate System

Lecture lines:
Distance in 2D is the Pythagorean hypotenuse.
In 3D, we add a depth squared term.
For n-dimensions, just sum all squared coordinates.
A sphere holds points at a fixed distance.
Equation: the sum of x_i squared equals radius squared.

Planned animations:
Display a 3D coordinate system. Color: #FFFFFF.
Highlight the axes origin with a bright glowing dot. Color: #FF00FF.
Transition to N-dimensional representation using a text label. Color: #00FFFF.

Section: section_2 — Defining the N-Sphere

Lecture lines:
An n-sphere exists in (n+1)-dimensional space.
The sphere's surface dimension is always n.
Example: a 2D circle is a 1-sphere.

Planned animations:
Display a sphere wireframe at center. Color: #FFFFFF.
Show radius vector r=1 emerging from center. Color: #FFFF00.
Flash the surface points where x^2+y^2+z^2=r^2. Color: #00FF00.

Section: section_3 — The Counter-Intuitive 'Empty' Center

Lecture lines:
Imagine a high-dimensional orange.
Almost all mass lives in the crust.
The core is effectively empty space.

Planned animations:
Show 2D circle with full shaded area. Color: #0000FF.
Show 3D sphere with mostly hollow interior. Color: #808080.
Highlight the thin shell volume of an N-sphere. Color: #FF4500.

Section: section_4 — The Curse of Dimensionality: Geometry in Data Science

Lecture lines:
In high dimensions, everything is far apart.
Distance metrics become unreliable for data.
Neighborhoods collapse in high-dimensional space.

Planned animations:
Show high-dimensional space as sparse points. Color: #FFFFFF.
Represent data clusters as shrinking spheres. Color: #FF6347.
Show increasing distance between points as dimensions grow. Color: #ADFF2F.

Section: section_5 — Summary and Conclusion

Lecture lines:
Our geometric intuition fails in high dimensions.
Mathematics reveals structures we cannot visualize.
High-dimensional spheres drive modern AI logic.

Planned animations:
Summarize core concepts with key text appearing. Color: #FFFFFF.
Flash the N-sphere volume formula briefly. Color: #FFD700.
Fade out all elements to black background. Color: #000000.

from manim import *

        # BASE

        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2

        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

from manim import *
import numpy as np

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section4Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("The Curse of Dimensionality", [
            "In high dimensions, everything is far apart.",
            "Distance metrics become unreliable for data.",
            "Neighborhoods collapse in high-dimensional space."
        ])
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # Show high-dimensional space as sparse points.
        points = VGroup(*[Dot(radius=0.05, color=WHITE) for _ in range(30)])
        for p in points:
            p.move_to(np.random.uniform(-2, 2, 3))
        
        self.place_in_area(points, 'A1', 'F6', scale_factor=1.0)
        self.play(Create(points))
        self.lecture[0].set_color("#FFFFFF")
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # Represent data clusters as shrinking spheres.
        sphere = Sphere(radius=1.5, color="#FF6347", fill_opacity=0.3)
        self.place_in_area(sphere, 'B2', 'E5', scale_factor=0.6)
        
        self.play(Create(sphere))
        self.play(sphere.animate.scale(0.5))
        self.lecture[1].set_color("#FF6347")
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # Show increasing distance between points as dimensions grow.
        dist_line = Line(start=self.grid['C2'], end=self.grid['D5'], color="#ADFF2F")
        dist_label = Text("d(x,y)", font_size=16, color="#ADFF2F")
        self.place_at_grid(dist_label, 'C4')
        
        self.play(Create(dist_line), Write(dist_label))
        self.play(dist_line.animate.stretch(1.5, 0))
        self.lecture[2].set_color("#ADFF2F")
        self.wait(2)

from manim import *
import numpy as np

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

    def construct(self):
        lecture_lines = [
            "An n-sphere exists in (n+1)-dimensional space.",
            "The sphere's surface dimension is always n.",
            "Example: a 2D circle is a 1-sphere."
        ]
        self.setup_layout("Defining the N-Sphere", lecture_lines)
        
        # Objects
        # Using [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/sphere.svg]
        sphere = SVGMobject("/scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/sphere.svg", color=WHITE)
        radius_vec = Arrow(start=ORIGIN, end=RIGHT*1.2, color=YELLOW)
        surface_label = Text("Surface(n)", font_size=20, color=CYAN_A)
        circle_highlight = Circle(radius=0.5, color=GOLD)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(BLUE))
        self.place_in_area(sphere, 'B3', 'E5', scale_factor=0.6)
        self.play(FadeIn(sphere))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(CYAN_A))
        self.place_at_grid(surface_label, 'F3', scale_factor=0.7)
        self.play(Write(surface_label))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color(GOLD))
        self.place_at_grid(radius_vec, 'C5', scale_factor=0.6)
        self.play(GrowArrow(radius_vec))
        self.place_at_grid(circle_highlight, 'C5', scale_factor=0.5)
        self.play(Create(circle_highlight))
        
        self.wait(2)
